vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: macro-helper
Version: 2.3.0

The macro-helper skill is a legitimate utility designed to assist users with Excel VBA development. The core logic in scripts/macro.sh consists of static text templates for code generation, debugging, and optimization, which are outputted via standard bash cat commands. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection; the skill operates entirely within its stated scope of providing VBA-related information and templates.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions are consistent with an Excel/VBA macro helper: it only contains local, read-only templates and guidance and does not request credentials or install external code.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the actual contents: the SKILL.md and scripts/macro.sh produce/generate/explain/debug/convert/optimize VBA code and templates. No unrelated binaries, environment variables, or cloud credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are limited: run bash scripts/macro.sh <command>. The script prints VBA templates, explanations, and debugging guidance. It does not instruct the agent to read arbitrary host files, access credentials, call external endpoints, or transmit data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided and the shipped shell script is local. There are no downloads or extract/install steps, so nothing external is pulled or executed during install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required environment variables, credentials, or config paths are declared or used. The script only uses its positional parameters and the local date command for timestamps.
dimensions.label: Credentials

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and local-only, but remember that the VBA macros it generates will run inside Excel and can perform powerful local actions (delete files, read/write workbooks, send email via Outlook, etc.). Before running any generated macro: review the VBA code line-by-line, remove or change any .Send calls to .Display for emails, verify attachment paths, and test in a sandbox or a copy of your workbook. The provided shell script itself only prints templates and does not exfiltrate data or require credentials. Note also there are minor truncation/typo artifacts in the shipped template file (e.g., an incomplete 'End S' near the end) — this looks like sloppy packaging rather than malicious behavior. If you want stronger assurance, ask the author for a full untruncated script and confirm the origin (bytesagain.com) before enabling autonomous execution.
